chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

When the deceased is placed in his grave, say: 'In the name of Allah and in the way of Allah and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Your servant, son of Your servant, has lodged with You, and You are the best of hosts. O Allah, make spacious for him in his grave and join him with his Prophet. O Allah, we do not know from him except good, and You are more knowing of him.'

So when you place the brick/slab upon him, say: 'O Allah, connect his loneliness and comfort his solitude, and settle upon him from Your mercy a mercy that suffices him from the mercy of anyone other than You.'

So when you leave his grave, say: 'We are from Allah and to Him we shall return, and the praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, raise his rank in the highest Illyin and succeed him among the remaining generations, O Lord of the worlds.'

key_terms.اللَّبِن: The brick or slab placed on top of the grave
key_terms.الْغَابِرِينَ: The remaining generations or those who survive after the deceased
key_terms.عِلِّيِّينَ: The highest register or realm, often associated with the abode of the righteous
key_terms.لَحْد: A rectangular grave pit with a side chamber, typical of Arab burial customs

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications to recite during the burial of the deceased in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith outlines the ritual etiquette (adab) of burial, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the deceased's immediate transition into the barzakh (intermediate realm). The supplications highlight key theological concepts such as the intercession of the Prophet, the sufficiency of divine mercy over creation, and the hope for high rank in 'Illiyin, serving as a spiritual bridge between the physical burial and the soul's journey.
